text: En un partido intenso del Northbridge League, Harbour City comenzó liderando 2-0 con goles de Elias Okafor y Marek Barros. Okafor marcó tras una larga jugada de 17 pases, mostrando la paciencia del equipo con su estilo de pases cortos [#905]. Sin embargo, Seabrook Town reaccionó rápido con un gol al minuto 53 de Tariq Marlowe, tras robar el balón y atacar rápido [#1104]. Con un cambio táctico al minuto 65, Seabrook presionó más y jugó directo, lo que les permitió empatar y posteriormente ganar el partido 4-2 [#1361] [#1882]. Kian Romano fue la estrella del final, anotando dos goles en los minutos 90+2 y 90+3, con una probabilidad de gol alta (xG 0.55 y 0.99), asegurando la victoria [#1882] [#1906]. Marek Barros brilló pese a la derrota, aportando gol y asistencias con una calificación perfecta de 10.0 [#975].

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in es

- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals with a high total xG of 3.53, significantly outperforming Harbour City's xG of 1.26 [#1882].
- Kian Romano scored twice in the final minutes (90+2' and 90+3') with very high xG values of 0.554 and 0.994, turning the match for Seabrook Town [#1882, #1906].
- Marek Barros was key for Harbour City, with 1 goal, 2 assists, 5 key passes, and a top rating of 10.0 despite his low xG of 0.9 [#975].
- Harbour City played with a patient short passing style in a 4-2-3-1 formation but had less possession (46.6%) and fewer shots (10) than Seabrook Town's 22 shots and 53.4% possession [overall stats].
- Seabrook Town changed tactics at 65' to press higher and play more direct, which preceded a comeback from 0-2 down to win 4-2 [#1361].

- Harbour City’s opening goal at 45' came after a sustained patient build-up involving 17 passes over nearly a minute, showing their 4-2-3-1 formation and patient short passing style maintaining possession before a through ball assist from Marek Barros allowed Elias Okafor to score from 11.7 meters, capitalizing on their possession-based approach [904,905].

- Marek Barros’ second goal at 47' originated from a corner, reflecting Harbour City's use of set pieces to create chances. The goal was scored on a low xG (0.029) chance, assisted by a cross from Barros himself following a short corner sequence, showing tactical set piece utilization under coach Tomasz Rhee [973,975].

- Seabrook Town's equalizer at 53' was a quick goal from Tariq Marlowe immediately upon regaining possession, reflecting a counter-attack pattern that suits their 3-4-3 formation and wide crossing, direct style. The rapid single-pass build-up from regaining possession highlights their ability to exploit turnovers and transition quickly [1103,1104].

- After tactical changes at 65’ initiated by Seabrook Town’s coach Mara Lindholm to press higher, play more direct, and increase line height, they improved attacking threat as seen in Callum Varga’s 69’ through-ball goal following a short 3-pass counter-attacking sequence starting from a regain. This adjustment reflects a shift from controlled build-up to exploiting quick transitions and wide play [1361,1447,1448].

- In the late stages, Seabrook Town’s goals at 90+2’ and 90+3’ illustrate effective counter-attacking and wide combination play. The first equalizing goal came from a fast break with a through ball assist by Aiden Quinlan for Kian Romano, while the subsequent go-ahead goal was built through short passes consistent with their wide crossing and direct style. This underscores their resilience and tactical efficiency exploiting high turnovers by Harbour City pressured in a higher defensive line [1881,1882,1905,1906].

Overall, Harbour City relied on patient possession with short passing and set pieces, consistent with their 4-2-3-1 style, while Seabrook Town effectively used wide, crossing play and pressing traps evolving into direct counter-attacks aligned with their 3-4-3 formation and tactical adjustments during the match.
